newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa in East Timor damage control.
newsitem.headline: South Africa in East Timor damage control.

text.p: South Africa, trying to unravel twin diplomatic blunders in its East Timor peace initiative, on Tuesday acknowledged a "miscommunication" over an announced visit by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

Presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana said a misunderstanding had led him and other government officials to announce that Annan would meet President Nelson Mandela in Pretoria on Friday to discuss a joint initiative for peace in Indonesian-controlled East Timor.
"There was a miscommunication with the United Nations and I must say the miscommunication appears to have been largely on our side," he told Reuters.
Mandela appeared on Tuesday to say that he still expected Annan on Friday, but an aide explained later that Mandela had misheard a reporter's question during a photo opportunity.
In a related development, the Foreign Ministry confirmed for the first time that South Africa asked Portugal last week to replace Ambassador Vasco Valente.

"...The government of Portugal (was) requested to bring forward the departure of Ambassador Vasco Valente, who was due to take up another diplomatic assignment, due to certain actions of the ambassador," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
"The department wishes to stress that these developments in no way reflect on the cordial relations that exist between South Africa and Portugal," the statement said.
It was the first official South African confirmation of reports by government sources that Valente had been expelled.
The sources alleged that Valente had leaked details of a letter from Mandela to President Suharto of Indonesia asking for the release of East Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao.
The letter was delivered to the Portuguese embassy in error.
Portugal said on Tuesday it would not retaliate in kind after the expulsion.
"We have no intention of asking for the expulsion of the South African ambassador to Lisbon," Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Ana Zacarias told Reuters.
Zacarias said Valente had thought the letter was a copy for his consideration.
Mandela wrote to Suharto in mid-July asking him to free Gusmao as a first step towards peace in the territory.
In a bungle not yet explained by South Africa, Mandela's letter was delivered to the Portuguese embassy and not to the Indonesian mission. It was neither returned nor forwarded.
Mandela became involved in the East Timor issue last month when he visited Suharto in Jakarta and met Gusmao.
He has since pledged his support for U.N. efforts to secure peace in East Timor and resolve the dispute over the territory's government.
Mankahlana said Annan had asked for an opportunity to visit Mandela and discuss the East Timor conflict, but not as at first thought in the immediate future.
South Africa now expected a visit from U.N. special representative Jamsheed Marker, who is heading talks in New York between Portugal and Indonesia, he said.
Mandela came under fire several years ago for accepting a huge donation to his now ruling African National Congress from Suharto without condemning his human rights record.
